content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_4/projects/trace-verdict-study/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — trace-verdict-study\\n\\n> v2.6 — [UPDATED 2026-05-15] 数据集来源纠正：非 CRUXEval，实为 HumanEval (164) + MBPP-sanitized (427) = 591 problems × 10 LLM-generated solutions = 5910 samples。CRUXEval 仅作为外部基准参照模型推理能力差异。\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR submission)\\n- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings\\n- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026\\n\\n## Core Insight\\n\\nVerdict prediction (pass/fail) is fundamentally a **fault detection** task. The minimal sufficient signal is the **exception event** — a compact, structured diagnostic moment that achieves near-perfect accuracy (Qwen 99.83%, DeepSeek 99.83% at best checkpoint, cross-model gap = 0pp) regardless of model architecture. In contrast, richer trace representations that require deeper execution reasoning show model-dependent effectiveness: VOTA gap = 14.96pp, no_trace gap = 1.77pp. Information density — not training signal distribution — is the primary bottleneck: even oracle loss masking (label-only) cannot close the 13pp gap between full traces and targeted extraction. The design principle: **extract the highest-specificity diagnostic signal; discard everything else.**\\n\\nVOTA's primary contribution is **fault indicator isolation** — automatically extracting exception events from noisy full traces — rather than generic trace compression. The \\\"compression helps\\\" narrative was a stepping stone; the real mechanism is diagnostic signal extraction.\\n\\n## Core Claims (3)\\n\\n### Claim 1: Exception-based fault detection is model-agnostic\\n\\nException summaries alone achieve near-perfect verdict prediction across architecturally distinct models: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B (99.83%) and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B (99.83% at epoch1 best), cross-model gap = 0pp at best checkpoint, 0.50pp at final checkpoint. This contrasts with VOTA (gap = 14.96pp) and no_trace (gap = 1.77pp). Exception events are structurally simple (`[ERROR] type: ... message: ...`) and do not require deep trace reasoning — making them universally extractable.\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`: Qwen 99.83%, ECE=0.0027\\n- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: DeepSeek 99.83% (epoch1 best) / 99.33% (epoch3 final)\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: DeepSeek VOTA 84.45% (gap = 14.96pp vs Qwen)\\n- `deepseek_no_trace_seed42`: DeepSeek no_trace 73.36% (gap = 1.77pp vs Qwen)\\n- `vota_no_ae_seed42`: 99.41% — actual/expected removal 不降，非 trivial string comparison\\n\\n**Seed robustness** ✅: Qwen exception_only 3-seed 完全一致，构成本文最强 robustness 证据：\\n\\n| Seed | Accuracy | 95% CI | Errors |\\n|------|----------|--------|--------|\\n| 42 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n| 123 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n| 456 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n\\n3 seeds 错误样本 100% 重叠（id=901, 905, 均为 `check_dict_case` 函数, label=pass → pred=fail）。**Irreducible samples**: 模型已达数据集理论上限，variance = 0。\\n\\n**DeepSeek cross-model**: epoch1 best checkpoint 99.83% 与 Qwen 完全一致（gap = 0pp），进一步确认 exception signal 的 universality。epoch3 退化至 99.33%（gap = 0.50pp），见 D7 early stopping 讨论。\\n\\n### Claim 2: Information density, not gradient dilution, drives trace compression benefit\\n\\nFull traces help verdict prediction (81.76% [`full_trace_seed42_v5`], +6.6pp over baseline), but VOTA achieves 99.41% [`vota_seed42_v5`] (+24.3pp) — a +17.6pp advantage. Label-only loss ablation (plan_002) quantifies the causal decomposition: **gradient dilution contributes ~26% of the gap** (4.5pp; label-only full_trace = 86.22% [`full_trace_label_only_seed42`]), **information overload contributes ~74%** (13.0pp; only trace compression resolves this). Even with oracle loss masking that eliminates gradient dilution, full traces still underperform VOTA by 13pp.\\n\\nCross-model evidence reinforces this: VOTA gap (14.96pp) tracks base model execution reasoning capability (Qwen CRUXEval-I 56.5% vs DeepSeek 39.0%, Δ=17.5pp), suggesting trace utilization effectiveness is bounded by pretraining-derived inductive biases. Exception signal bypasses this bottleneck entirely (gap = 0pp at best checkpoint).\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.22%, ECE=0.1107 (gradient dilution fix, +4.5pp over standard full_trace)\\n- `full_trace_seed42_v5`: 81.76%, ECE=0.0958 (standard full_trace)\\n- `vota_seed42_v5`: 99.41%, ECE=0.0054\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (VOTA model-dependent)\\n- CRUXEval literature data (Wang et al.)\\n\\n### Claim 3: Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy for verdict prediction\\n\\nComponent ablation reveals verdict-relevant trace information has a strict two-tier hierarchy:\\n- **Tier 1 — diagnostic moment signals**: exception summaries (99.83% [`vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`]) and assertion-point information (99.92% [`vota_ae_only_seed42`]) are individually near-perfect and sufficient for verdict prediction. These signals are structurally simple and model-agnostic (exception cross-model gap = 0pp at best checkpoint).\\n- **Tier 2 — behavioral patterns**: loop compression (85.63% [`vota_loop_only_seed42`]) carries substantial signal but is model-dependent and fully subsumed by Tier 1.\\n\\nCombining tiers introduces noise rather than helping: exception_only (99.83%) > VOTA full (99.41%), p=0.01. Loop_only ≈ full_trace_label_only (85.63% vs 86.22%) confirms VOTA's loop compression precisely extracts the useful behavioral signal from full traces.\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`: 99.83%, ECE=0.0027 (Tier 1 exception)\\n- `vota_ae_only_seed42`: 99.92%, ECE=0.0004 (Tier 1 assertion-point, 与 exception 统计等价 p=0.80)\\n- `vota_loop_only_seed42`: 85.63%, ECE=0.0831 (Tier 2 behavioral)\\n- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.22%, ECE=0.1107 (≈ loop_only, confirming extraction equivalence)\\n- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: 99.83% epoch1 / 99.33% epoch3 (Tier 1 cross-model validation)\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (Tier 1+2 cross-model: Tier 2 introduces model-dependent degradation)\\n\\n**Calibration**: 完整 calibration 数据确认 Tier 1 信号不仅 accuracy 近完美，置信度校准也近完美：\\n\\n| Condition | Accuracy | ECE | Brier | 解读 |\\n|-----------|----------|-----|-------|------|\\n| ae_only | 99.92% | 0.0004 | 0.0008 | 近乎完美校准 |\\n| exception_only | 99.83% | 0.0027 | 0.0013 | 近乎完美校准 |\\n| VOTA | 99.41% | 0.0054 | 0.005 | 优秀，但 Tier 2 引入轻微 noise |\\n| loop_only | 85.63% | 0.0831 | — | Tier 2 单独校准中等 |\\n| label_only | 86.22% | 0.1107 | — | gradient dilution fix 仍 miscalibrated |\\n| full_trace | 81.76% | 0.0958 | — | 中度 miscalibrated |\\n| no_trace | 75.13% | 0.1715 | 0.1972 | 严重 miscalibrated |\\n\\nno_trace ECE 是 exception_only 的 **~63x**（0.1715/0.0027），Brier 是 **~150x**（0.1972/0.0013）。Trace signal（尤其 Tier 1）不仅提升 accuracy，更从根本上改善模型 calibration。\\n\\n**Design principle**: verdict-optimized traces should extract highest-specificity diagnostic signals; lower-specificity signals are redundant and may introduce noise.\\n\\n## Cross-Model Evidence Summary\\n\\n| Condition | Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B | DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B | Cross-model gap | Interpretation |\\n|-----------|-------------------|---------------------|-----------------|----------------|\\n| exception_only | 99.83% | 99.83% (ep1) / 99.33% (ep3) | 0pp (best) / 0.50pp (final) | **Universal** — model-agnostic |\\n| VOTA | 99.41% | 84.45% | -14.96pp | Model-dependent — requires execution reasoning |\\n| no_trace | 75.13% | 73.36% | -1.77pp | Baseline gap tracks general capability |\\n| full_trace | 81.76% | collapsed (v3 pending) | N/A | DeepSeek v1 label truncation bug |\\n\\n**Key insight**: cross-model gap 与 signal complexity 正相关。Structurally simple signals (exception) transfer perfectly; signals requiring execution reasoning (VOTA loop compression) degrade proportional to CRUXEval reasoning gap (17.5pp).\\n\\n## VOTA Repositioning\\n\\n**旧叙事**: VOTA 是 trace compression 方法，价值在于\\\"压缩使 trace 更有效\\\"。\\n\\n**新叙事**: VOTA 是 **fault indicator isolation** 方法，核心价值在于自动从 noisy execution traces 中提取 exception events 等 diagnostic signals。\\n\\n**证据链**:\\n1. exception_only (99.83%) ≥ VOTA full (99.41%) — 压缩后的其他组件（loop, ae）不仅无益，反而引入 noise\\n2. > v2.6 — [UPDATED 2026-05-15] 数据集来源纠正：非 CRUXEval，实为 HumanEval (164) + MBPP-sanitized (427) = 591 problems × 10 LLM-generated solutions = 5910 samples。CRUXEval 仅作为外部基准参照模型推理能力差异。

## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR submission)
- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings
- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026

## Core Insight

Verdict prediction (pass/fail) is fundamentally a **fault detection** task. The minimal sufficient signal is the **exception event** — a compact, structured diagnostic moment that achieves near-perfect accuracy (Qwen 99.83%, DeepSeek 99.83% at best checkpoint, cross-model gap = 0pp) regardless of model architecture. In contrast, richer trace representations that require deeper execution reasoning show model-dependent effectiveness: VOTA gap = 14.96pp, no_trace gap = 1.77pp. Information density — not training signal distribution — is the primary bottleneck: even oracle loss masking (label-only) cannot close the 13pp gap between full traces and targeted extraction. The design principle: **extract the highest-specificity diagnostic signal; discard everything else.**

VOTA's primary contribution is **fault indicator isolation** — automatically extracting exception events from noisy full traces — rather than generic trace compression. The "compression helps" narrative was a stepping stone; the real mechanism is diagnostic signal extraction.

## Core Claims (3)

### Claim 1: Exception-based fault detection is model-agnostic

Exception summaries alone achieve near-perfect verdict prediction across architecturally distinct models: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B (99.83%) and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B (99.83% at epoch1 best), cross-model gap = 0pp at best checkpoint, 0.50pp at final checkpoint. This contrasts with VOTA (gap = 14.96pp) and no_trace (gap = 1.77pp). Exception events are structurally simple (`[ERROR] type: ... message: ...`) and do not require deep trace reasoning — making them universally extractable.

**Supporting evidence:**
- `vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`: Qwen 99.83%, ECE=0.0027
- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: DeepSeek 99.83% (epoch1 best) / 99.33% (epoch3 final)
- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: DeepSeek VOTA 84.45% (gap = 14.96pp vs Qwen)
- `deepseek_no_trace_seed42`: DeepSeek no_trace 73.36% (gap = 1.77pp vs Qwen)
- `vota_no_ae_seed42`: 99.41% — actual/expected removal 不降，非 trivial string comparison

**Seed robustness** ✅: Qwen exception_only 3-seed 完全一致，构成本文最强 robustness 证据：

| Seed | Accuracy | 95% CI | Errors |
|------|----------|--------|--------|
| 42 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |
| 123 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |
| 456 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |

3 seeds 错误样本 100% 重叠（id=901, 905, 均为 `check_dict_case` 函数, label=pass → pred=fail）。**Irreducible samples**: 模型已达数据集理论上限，variance = 0。

**DeepSeek cross-model**: epoch1 best checkpoint 99.83% 与 Qwen 完全一致（gap = 0pp），进一步确认 exception signal 的 universality。epoch3 退化至 99.33%（gap = 0.50pp），见 D7 early stopping 讨论。

### Claim 2: Information density, not gradient dilution, drives trace compression benefit

Full traces help verdict prediction (81.76% [`full_trace_seed42_v5`], +6.6pp over baseline), but VOTA achieves 99.41% [`vota_seed42_v5`] (+24.3pp) — a +17.6pp advantage. Label-only loss ablation (plan_002) quantifies the causal decomposition: **gradient dilution contributes ~26% of the gap** (4.5pp; label-only full_trace = 86.22% [`full_trace_label_only_seed42`]), **information overload contributes ~74%** (13.0pp; only trace compression resolves this). Even with oracle loss masking that eliminates gradient dilution, full traces still underperform VOTA by 13pp.

Cross-model evidence reinforces this: VOTA gap (14.96pp) tracks base model execution reasoning capability (Qwen CRUXEval-I 56.5% vs DeepSeek 39.0%, Δ=17.5pp), suggesting trace utilization effectiveness is bounded by pretraining-derived inductive biases. Exception signal bypasses this bottleneck entirely (gap = 0pp at best checkpoint).

**Supporting evidence:**
- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.22%, ECE=0.1107 (gradient dilution fix, +4.5pp over standard full_trace)
- `full_trace_seed42_v5`: 81.76%, ECE=0.0958 (standard full_trace)
- `vota_seed42_v5`: 99.41%, ECE=0.0054
- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (VOTA model-dependent)
- CRUXEval literature data (Wang et al.)

### Claim 3: Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy for verdict prediction

Component ablation reveals verdict-relevant trace information has a strict two-tier hierarchy:
- **Tier 1 — diagnostic moment signals**: exception summaries (99.83% [`vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`]) and assertion-point information (99.92% [`vota_ae_only_seed42`]) are individually near-perfect and sufficient for verdict prediction. These signals are structurally simple and model-agnostic (exception cross-model gap = 0pp at best checkpoint).
- **Tier 2 — behavioral patterns**: loop compression (85.63% [`vota_loop_only_seed42`]) carries substantial signal but is model-dependent and fully subsumed by Tier 1.

Combining tiers introduces noise rather than helping: exception_only (99.83%) > VOTA full (99.41%), p=0.01. Loop_only ≈ full_trace_label_only (85.63% vs 86.22%) confirms VOTA's loop compression precisely extracts the useful behavioral signal from full traces.

**Supporting evidence:**
- `vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`: 99.83%, ECE=0.0027 (Tier 1 exception)
- `vota_ae_only_seed42`: 99.92%, ECE=0.0004 (Tier 1 assertion-point, 与 exception 统计等价 p=0.80)
- `vota_loop_only_seed42`: 85.63%, ECE=0.0831 (Tier 2 behavioral)
- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.22%, ECE=0.1107 (≈ loop_only, confirming extraction equivalence)
- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: 99.83% epoch1 / 99.33% epoch3 (Tier 1 cross-model validation)
- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (Tier 1+2 cross-model: Tier 2 introduces model-dependent degradation)

**Calibration**: 完整 calibration 数据确认 Tier 1 信号不仅 accuracy 近完美，置信度校准也近完美：

| Condition | Accuracy | ECE | Brier | 解读 |
|-----------|----------|-----|-------|------|
| ae_only | 99.92% | 0.0004 | 0.0008 | 近乎完美校准 |
| exception_only | 99.83% | 0.0027 | 0.0013 | 近乎完美校准 |
| VOTA | 99.41% | 0.0054 | 0.005 | 优秀，但 Tier 2 引入轻微 noise |
| loop_only | 85.63% | 0.0831 | — | Tier 2 单独校准中等 |
| label_only | 86.22% | 0.1107 | — | gradient dilution fix 仍 miscalibrated |
| full_trace | 81.76% | 0.0958 | — | 中度 miscalibrated |
| no_trace | 75.13% | 0.1715 | 0.1972 | 严重 miscalibrated |

no_trace ECE 是 exception_only 的 **~63x**（0.1715/0.0027），Brier 是 **~150x**（0.1972/0.0013）。Trace signal（尤其 Tier 1）不仅提升 accuracy，更从根本上改善模型 calibration。

**Design principle**: verdict-optimized traces should extract highest-specificity diagnostic signals; lower-specificity signals are redundant and may introduce noise.

## Cross-Model Evidence Summary

| Condition | Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B | DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B | Cross-model gap | Interpretation |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------------|-----------------|----------------|
| exception_only | 99.83% | 99.83% (ep1) / 99.33% (ep3) | 0pp (best) / 0.50pp (final) | **Universal** — model-agnostic |
| VOTA | 99.41% | 84.45% | -14.96pp | Model-dependent — requires execution reasoning |
| no_trace | 75.13% | 73.36% | -1.77pp | Baseline gap tracks general capability |
| full_trace | 81.76% | collapsed (v3 pending) | N/A | DeepSeek v1 label truncation bug |

**Key insight**: cross-model gap 与 signal complexity 正相关。Structurally simple signals (exception) transfer perfectly; signals requiring execution reasoning (VOTA loop compression) degrade proportional to CRUXEval reasoning gap (17.5pp).

## VOTA Repositioning

**旧叙事**: VOTA 是 trace compression 方法，价值在于"压缩使 trace 更有效"。

**新叙事**: VOTA 是 **fault indicator isolation** 方法，核心价值在于自动从 noisy execution traces 中提取 exception events 等 diagnostic signals。

**证据链**:
1. exception_only (99.83%) ≥ VOTA full (99.41%) — 压缩后的其他组件（loop, ae）不仅无益，反而引入 noise
2. VOTA 跨模型 gap = 14.96pp — 因为 VOTA 包含 model-dependent 的 Tier 2 组件（loop compression 需要 execution reasoning）
3. exception_only 跨模型 gap = 0pp — isolate 出 Tier 1 后，model capability 不再是瓶颈
4. vota_no_ae (99.41%) = VOTA (99.41%) — actual/expected 移除无影响，exception 是真正的 active ingredient

**论文中的表述**: "VOTA's trace compression pipeline incidentally isolates exception events — the minimal sufficient diagnostic signal. Its value lies not in making traces shorter, but in separating high-specificity fault indicators from low-specificity behavioral patterns."

**对 Method section 的影响**: VOTA 仍然完整描述（loop compression + exception + actual/expected），但 Results/Discussion 明确指出 exception isolation 是核心机制，其他组件是 model-capability-dependent bonus。

## Story Spine

- **Problem**: Existing trace SFT studies (DCSH, TracePile) evaluate only generative tasks and find limited, model-dependent benefit. No prior work has tested trace SFT on verdict tasks (binary pass/fail), nor identified what trace components drive classification performance.

- **Existing approaches & gaps**: DCSH (EMNLP Findings 2025) tested 5 trace formats on generation tasks, finding that "no single trace representation consistently outperforms others." TracePile (NeurIPS 2025) scaled to 2.6M samples but only evaluated generation. TRACED (ICSE 2024) showed traces help encoder-based classification. All existing trace formats are designed for execution simulation, not fault detection.

- **Our framing**: We reframe verdict prediction as **fault detection** and ask: what is the minimal sufficient diagnostic signal? Through systematic component ablation across two architecturally distinct models, we discover that exception events — compact, structured error summaries — are both necessary and sufficient, achieving near-perfect accuracy (99.83% on both models at best checkpoint) with zero cross-model gap. Richer trace representations work only when the base model has sufficient execution reasoning capability, making them unreliable for general deployment.

- **Headline result**: "Exception events achieve 99.83% verdict accuracy on both Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B (cross-model gap = 0pp), while VOTA traces show a 14.96pp gap between the same models — demonstrating that fault indicator isolation, not trace reasoning, is the robust mechanism for verdict prediction."

## Story Arc

1. **Setup**: Trace SFT for code tasks — promising but inconsistent in prior work (DCSH, TracePile). Unknown whether traces help verdict tasks and what trace design matters.

2. **First result — traces help, compression helps more** (single model): no_trace 75.13% → full_trace 81.76% → VOTA 99.41%. Label-only loss ablation decomposes the gap: 26% gradient dilution, 74% information overload. Compression improves accuracy through higher information density, not just cost savings.

3. **Twist — what component actually drives VOTA?** Component ablation reveals exception_only (99.83%) ≥ full VOTA (99.41%). The "trace reasoning" narrative is wrong — verdict prediction is fault detection. Tier 1 (exceptions + assertion-point) subsumes Tier 2 (loops). Actual/expected removal doesn't hurt (99.41%).

4. **Cross-model stress test — the universal vs the contingent**: Exception_only transfers with zero gap (0pp at best checkpoint), but VOTA degrades by 14.96pp on DeepSeek. The model-agnostic component is precisely the one that doesn't require trace reasoning. CRUXEval reasoning gap (17.5pp) parallels VOTA gap — trace utilization is bounded by pretraining. Seed robustness (3-seed variance = 0) + calibration (ECE=0.0027) 双重确认 exception signal 的 reliability。

5. **Design principle**: For verdict tasks, identify the highest-specificity diagnostic signal (exception events) and discard everything else. VOTA's value is fault indicator isolation — automatically extracting exceptions from noisy traces — not generic compression. Simpler signals are more robust; complexity tolerance depends on model capability.

## DeepSeek full_trace 处理

**处理方案**: 下一个 GPU 空闲（deepseek_exception_only_seed123 完成后 ~20:15 UTC）立即重启 deepseek_full_trace_v3。

**对论文叙事的影响**: 无. 三个有效条件 (exception_only, VOTA, no_trace) 已足够支撑全部 claims. DeepSeek full_trace 结果是 bonus, 非必需. 若 v3 在投稿前完成, 纳入跨模型对比表 (4/4 conditions). 否则报告为 N/A 并在 Limitations 中透明披露根因.

| Concern | Planned Response |
|---------|-----------------|

### D1: eval_loss vs verdict accuracy 解耦

### D2: CRUXEval gap 假说
VOTA 跨模型 gap (14.96pp) 与 CRUXEval execution reasoning gap (15-17.5pp) 数值吻合. 假说: trace utilization effectiveness 受 base model "execution reasoning readiness" 约束. **标注**: hypothesis, N=2, 列出 alternatives. 不 overclaim. **注意**: 我们的训练/测试数据来自 HumanEval + MBPP-sanitized（非 CRUXEval），CRUXEval-I 分数仅作为衡量两个模型 execution reasoning 能力差异的外部参照。

### D3: Simplicity as robustness
Exception signal 跨模型 robust 恰因其 structurally simple. 暗示 **trace design 应匹配 deployment model 的能力下界**, 而非上界.

### D4: Checkpoint selection 与 gap 报告
正文 exception_only 跨模型 gap 用 final-to-final = 0.50pp (一致 criterion). 补充: at best checkpoint (DeepSeek epoch1), gap = 0pp. DeepSeek epoch1→3 退化 0.50pp 与 D1 eval_loss 解耦现象一致.

DeepSeek exception_only: epoch1 = 99.83%, epoch3 = 99.33%（退化 0.50pp）。Exception signal 结构简单，1 epoch 即充分学习；延长训练导致 token-level overfitting 反而轻微损害 binary classification。与 D1 的 eval_loss 解耦现象一致。**Implication**: 对 structurally simple diagnostic signals，early stopping 不仅节省计算，可能还提升性能。论文建议: verdict SFT 应 monitor task-specific metric (accuracy) 而非 training loss，尤其当训练信号高度 structured 时。对比: VOTA 在 DeepSeek 上 epoch1→3 accuracy 持续上升 (78.15%→84.45%)，说明 complex signals 确实需要更多 epochs——early stopping 的最优点取决于 signal complexity。

This is very revealing! The data generation pipeline is:

1. Load problems from HumanEval (164 problems) + MBPP sanitized (let me check how many)
2. For each problem, generate `n_samples` solutions using Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (default n=10)
3. Execute each solution with trace and record pass/fail

So the expansion is: each function gets 10 (default) sampled solutions, each of which may pass or fail. This means the "800 Python functions" expand to ~5910 samples because each function has multiple generated solutions, not multiple test inputs.
 
Wait, there's a discrepancy here. The paper claims CRUXEval with 800 functions, but the actual code is pulling from HumanEval and MBPP instead. HumanEval has 164 problems and MBPP sanitized has around 427, which only adds up to roughly 591 total — nowhere near 800. So either the paper's description doesn't match the implementation, or there's something else going on with how the data is being counted. Looking at the actual data structure, each line has the same problem ID and input text, but the output is consistently "pass" with no exception trace. The input field contains the function code and test assertions, so I need to examine whether the solutions themselves are actually identical or if there's something else going on with how the data was generated.

This reveals a potential data quality issue — if there are many exact duplicates, the effective training set is smaller than reported, which could lead to overfitting. More importantly, the paper seems to misrepresent the data source as CRUXEval when it's actually using HumanEval + MBPP with multiple LLM-generated solutions per function (some passing, some failing), not multiple test inputs per function. I should check the format_training_data.py script to understand how the raw traces are processed into the final training data.

Now I'm noticing the problem_id "MBPP/730" in the data, which confirms this is from MBPP rather than CRUXEval as claimed. CRUXEval itself is based on HumanEval and MBPP but focuses on input/output prediction, not verdict prediction. The writing plan mentions DCSH (Wang et al.) constructed a verdict prediction version from CRUXEval, but I need to verify whether that's actually what's being used here or if there's a mismatch between the claimed and actual data sources.

Looking at the generate_data.py code, it's directly loading HumanEval and MBPP independently and generating solutions with vLLM, which suggests either the pipeline was rewritten after the paper was written, or the paper's description doesn't accurately reflect the implementation. This is a critical discrepancy that needs clarification. I should also check format_training_data.py to see if there's any CRUXEval reference or deduplication logic there.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	
3	We evaluate our trace preprocessing pipeline across two research questions:
4	(1)~Do Tier~1 exception signals generalize across models of different capability?
5	(2)~What is the relative contribution of each trace component to verdict prediction accuracy?
6	All experiments use our trace--verdict dataset (\S\ref{sec:dataset}) with $N{=}1{,}190$ test samples; accuracy is reported with Wilson 95\% confidence intervals unless stated otherwise.
7	Pairwise comparisons use paired bootstrap resampling ($B{=}10{,}000$, seed=42); all cross-condition differences reported below are significant at $p{<}0.0001$ unless noted otherwise.
8	
9	\subsection{Cross-Model Comparison}
10	\label{sec:cross_model}
11	
12	To test whether exception-based trace compression transfers across model families, we compare Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct under four input conditions: \texttt{exception\_only} (Tier~1 exception events), VOTA (exception + assertion-point + loop compression), \texttt{full\_trace} (complete execution trace), and \texttt{no\_trace} (source code only).
13	
14	\begin{table}[t]
15	\centering
16	\small
17	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
18	\toprule
19	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Qwen-2.5-7B} & \textbf{DeepSeek-6.7B} & \textbf{Gap} \\
20	\midrule
21	exception\_only & \textbf{99.83}\% & 99.33\%$^\dag$ & 0.50pp \\
22	VOTA & 99.41\% & 84.45\% & 14.96pp \\
23	VOTA\_no\_ae & 99.41\%$^\S$ & --- & --- \\
24	full\_trace & 81.76\% & N/A$^\ddag$ & --- \\
25	no\_trace & 75.13\% & 73.36\% & 1.77pp \\
26	\midrule
27	Majority baseline & 71.51\% & 71.51\% & --- \\
28	\bottomrule
29	\end{tabular}
30	\caption{Cross-model accuracy ($N{=}1{,}190$). Qwen CIs: exception\_only [99.58, 100.00], VOTA [98.82, 99.83], full\_trace [79.70, 83.90], no\_trace [72.77, 77.48]; DeepSeek CIs: VOTA [82.60, 86.40], no\_trace [70.80, 75.70]. $^\dag$DeepSeek exception\_only reached 99.83\% at epoch~1 but degraded to 99.33\% at convergence (single seed, no CI). $^\S$VOTA\_no\_ae evaluated on Qwen only; CI [98.90, 99.80]. $^\ddag$DeepSeek full\_trace was invalidated because the DeepSeek tokenizer produced sequences exceeding 2{,}048 tokens, causing the verdict label to be truncated during training; the model consequently failed to learn the classification task.}
31	\label{tab:cross_model}
32	\end{table}
33	
34	Table~\ref{tab:cross_model} reveals a striking asymmetry.
35	Under \texttt{exception\_only}, the cross-model gap is only 0.50 percentage points (pp), indicating that exception events carry a near-sufficient signal regardless of model capacity.
36	Under VOTA, the gap widens to 14.96pp: DeepSeek drops to 84.45\% while Qwen remains at 99.41\%.
37	This pattern suggests that processing mixed trace components (loop compressions, assertion points) demands model capability that the smaller DeepSeek lacks, whereas isolated exception events are interpretable by both models.
38	Per-class analysis (Appendix~\ref{sec:per_class}) reveals the mechanism: DeepSeek VOTA achieves 100\% fail precision but only 45.43\% fail recall, systematically defaulting to \texttt{pass}---in contrast to Qwen VOTA, which achieves 100\% fail recall.
39	
40	The \texttt{no\_trace} baseline confirms that source code alone provides limited signal (75.13\% for Qwen, 73.36\% for DeepSeek), only marginally above majority-class guessing (71.51\%).
41	
42	Seed robustness for Qwen \texttt{exception\_only} was evaluated across three seeds (42, 123, 456): all three produced identical accuracy of 99.83\% with exactly two errors each ($\sigma{=}0$, $n{=}3$).
43	
44	\subsection{Component Ablation}
45	\label{sec:ablation}
46	
47	We decompose the VOTA pipeline into individual components on Qwen-2.5-7B (seed=42).
48	Table~\ref{tab:ablation} arranges conditions into a two-tier hierarchy: Tier~1 signals (\texttt{ae\_only}, \texttt{exception\_only}) that individually achieve ${\geq}$99.8\% accuracy, and Tier~2 signals (\texttt{loop\_only}) that provide moderate improvement over the no-trace baseline.
49	
50	\begin{table}[t]
51	\centering
52	\small
53	\begin{tabular}{llccc}
54	\toprule
55	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Components} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} & \textbf{95\% CI} & \textbf{Tier} \\
56	\midrule
57	ae\_only & assertion-point & \textbf{99.92} & [99.75, 100.00] & 1 \\
58	exception\_only & exception events & 99.83 & [99.58, 100.00] & 1 \\
59	VOTA & exc+ae+loop & 99.41 & [98.82, 99.83] & --- \\
60	VOTA\_no\_ae & exc+loop & 99.41 & [98.90, 99.80] & --- \\
61	loop\_only & loop compression & 85.63 & [83.53, 87.56] & 2 \\
62	full\_trace & complete trace & 81.76 & [79.70, 83.90] & --- \\
63	no\_trace & none & 75.13 & [72.77, 77.48] & --- \\
64	\bottomrule
65	\end{tabular}
66	\caption{Component ablation on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$, seed=42). Tier~1 signals individually achieve near-perfect accuracy; combining them (VOTA) slightly dilutes performance.}
67	\label{tab:ablation}
68	\end{table}
69	
70	Two findings stand out.
71	First, the Tier~1 signals are individually sufficient: \texttt{ae\_only} (99.92\%) and \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%) are not distinguishable ($p{=}0.80$, paired bootstrap, $B{=}10{,}000$), and both exceed VOTA (99.41\%, $p{=}0.01$ for \texttt{exception\_only} vs.\ VOTA, paired bootstrap).
72	This implies that combining signals in VOTA introduces minor noise rather than complementary information.
73	Second, removing assertion points from VOTA has no effect (VOTA\_no\_ae = VOTA = 99.41\%), confirming that within the VOTA mixture, exception events dominate the prediction signal.
74	
75	Tier~2 signal \texttt{loop\_only} (85.63\%) improves over \texttt{no\_trace} (75.13\%) by 10.50pp ($p{<}0.0001$, bootstrap 95\% CI $[{+}8.24, {+}12.86]$), showing that loop compression captures some execution semantics, but far less than exception events.
76	
77	\subsection{Information Density Decomposition}
78	\label{sec:density}
79	
80	The gap between \texttt{full\_trace} (81.76\%) and VOTA (99.41\%) is 17.65pp.
81	We decompose this gap into two mechanisms by introducing an intermediate condition, \texttt{full\_trace\_label\_only}, which retains the complete trace as input but computes loss only on the verdict token, masking all trace tokens during training.
82	
83	\begin{table}[t]
84	\centering
85	\small
86	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
87	\toprule
88	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} & \textbf{$\Delta$ vs.\ full\_trace} & \textbf{Gap explained} \\
89	\midrule
90	full\_trace & 81.76 & --- & --- \\
91	label\_only & 86.22 & +4.46pp & 26\% \\
92	VOTA & 99.41 & +17.65pp & 100\% \\
93	\bottomrule
94	\end{tabular}
95	\caption{Information density decomposition. The full\_trace$\to$VOTA gap decomposes into gradient dilution (26\%, addressed by masking trace tokens from the loss) and information overload (74\%, addressed by removing irrelevant trace lines via VOTA compression).}
96	\label{tab:density}
97	\end{table}
98	
99	As shown in Table~\ref{tab:density}, the decomposition attributes 26\% of the gap (+4.46pp, $p{<}0.0001$, bootstrap 95\% CI $[{+}2.35, {+}6.55]$) to \emph{gradient dilution}---the training signal is diluted across trace tokens that do not contribute to verdict prediction---and 74\% (+13.19pp) to \emph{information overload}---the model must process trace lines irrelevant to the fault at inference time.
100	This two-factor decomposition is consistent across models: the VOTA cross-model gap (14.96pp, Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) tracks model capability, suggesting that weaker models are disproportionately affected by information overload.
101	
102	\subsection{Calibration Analysis}
103	\label{sec:calibration}
104	
105	Beyond accuracy, we evaluate whether trace conditions affect prediction calibration, motivated by recent findings that code LLM confidence is often poorly calibrated \citep{spiess2025calibration}.
106	Figure~\ref{fig:calibration} shows reliability diagrams for four conditions on Qwen-2.5-7B.
107	
108	\begin{table}[t]
109	\centering
110	\small
111	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
112	\toprule
113	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{ECE $\downarrow$} & \textbf{Brier $\downarrow$} \\
114	\midrule
115	ae\_only & \textbf{0.0004} & \textbf{0.0008} \\
116	exception\_only & 0.003 & 0.0013 \\
117	VOTA & 0.005 & 0.005 \\
118	full\_trace & 0.096 & 0.144 \\
119	no\_trace & 0.171 & 0.197 \\
120	\bottomrule
121	\end{tabular}
122	\caption{Calibration metrics on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$, seed=42). ECE = expected calibration error; Brier = Brier score. Lower is better for both.}
123	\label{tab:calibration}
124	\end{table}
125	
126	Table~\ref{tab:calibration} shows that calibration quality mirrors the Tier~1/2 hierarchy.
127	Tier~1 conditions (\texttt{ae\_only}: ECE=0.0004; \texttt{exception\_only}: ECE=0.003) produce near-perfectly calibrated predictions, while \texttt{full\_trace} (ECE=0.096) and \texttt{no\_trace} (ECE=0.171) exhibit substantial miscalibration.
128	VOTA (ECE=0.005) is well-calibrated but slightly worse than either Tier~1 component alone, reinforcing the pattern that combining trace signals dilutes rather than improves the prediction signal.
129	
130	The Brier scores tell a consistent story: \texttt{ae\_only} (0.0008) and \texttt{exception\_only} (0.0013) achieve near-zero scores, while \texttt{no\_trace} (0.197) indicates substantial miscalibration.
131	
132	Figure~\ref{fig:cross_model_gap} visualizes the cross-model gap pattern, showing that exception-based conditions maintain tight cross-model agreement while VOTA and lower-tier conditions diverge.
133	
134	\begin{figure}[t]
135	\centering
136	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig2_calibration}
137	\caption{Reliability diagrams for four trace conditions on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$, seed=42). The Tier~1 condition (\texttt{exception\_only}) clusters near the diagonal (well-calibrated), while \texttt{full\_trace} and \texttt{no\_trace} exhibit systematic overconfidence.}
138	\label{fig:calibration}
139	\end{figure}
140	
141	\begin{figure}[t]
142	\centering
143	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig3_cross_model_gap}
144	\caption{Cross-model accuracy gap (Qwen $-$ DeepSeek) across trace conditions. Exception-based signals transfer across models (0.50pp gap), while VOTA is model-dependent (14.96pp gap).}
145	\label{fig:cross_model_gap}
146	\end{figure}

1	\section{Introduction}
2	
3	Execution traces---line-by-line records of a program's runtime behavior---have emerged as a promising input modality for code language models.
4	Recent work has explored trace-augmented training for code generation \citep{chen2025tracepile}, execution-aware pretraining \citep{ding2024traced}, trace-based code understanding \citep{wang2025dcsh}, and self-training on trace chain-of-thought \citep{ni2024next}.
5	Yet a fundamental question remains open: \emph{which components of an execution trace actually matter?}
6	
7	\citet{wang2025dcsh} found that no single trace representation consistently outperforms others on generation-oriented tasks, concluding that the utility of execution traces is task- and format-dependent.
8	However, their study focused on code generation and repair---tasks that require the model to simulate or reconstruct execution semantics.
9	\emph{Verdict prediction}---classifying whether a test passes or fails---is a fundamentally different task type: it is a fault detection problem, not a generation problem.
10	Whether the same trace components matter for fault detection as for generation is unknown.
11	
12	We present the first systematic study of what trace components drive verdict prediction performance.
13	Using 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} and MBPP-sanitized \citep{austin2021program} with model-generated solutions and execution traces, we decompose a multi-component trace representation (VOTA: exception events + assertion-point comparisons + loop compression) into individual components and evaluate each in isolation across two models: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct.
14	
15	Our results reveal a striking finding: \textbf{exception events alone are sufficient for near-perfect verdict prediction, and this signal transfers across model families.}
16	With only exception events as trace input, both models achieve ${\geq}$99.3\% accuracy (cross-model gap = 0.50 percentage points).
17	In contrast, the full VOTA representation---which combines exception events with assertion-point and loop information---degrades by 14.96pp on the weaker model, indicating that processing mixed trace components demands model capability that exception-only prediction does not.
18	
19	These results reframe verdict prediction as fault detection: the minimal sufficient signal is the exception event, a compact structured diagnostic moment that both models can interpret without deep trace reasoning.
20	We further decompose the gap between full trace and VOTA into two mechanisms---\emph{gradient dilution} (26\% of the gap) and \emph{information overload} (74\%)---showing that the primary bottleneck is not training signal quality but the presence of irrelevant trace content.
21	
22	Our contributions are:
23	\begin{enumerate}
24	\item \textbf{Exception signal universality}: We show that exception events alone achieve 99.83\%/99.33\% accuracy across two models (gap = 0.50pp), while VOTA degrades 14.96pp on the weaker model (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
25	\item \textbf{Information density decomposition}: We decompose the full-trace-to-VOTA gap into gradient dilution (26\%) and information overload (74\%), identifying the primary bottleneck for trace-based prediction (\S\ref{sec:density}).
26	\item \textbf{Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy}: Component ablation reveals that Tier~1 signals (exception events, assertion points) individually achieve ${\geq}$99.8\% accuracy while Tier~2 signals (loop compression) reach only 85.6\% (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).
27	\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}

Execution traces---line-by-line records of a program's runtime behavior---have emerged as a promising input modality for code language models.
Recent work has explored trace-augmented training for code generation \citep{chen2025tracepile}, execution-aware pretraining \citep{ding2024traced}, trace-based code understanding \citep{wang2025dcsh}, and self-training on trace chain-of-thought \citep{ni2024next}.
Yet a fundamental question remains open: \emph{which components of an execution trace actually matter?}

\citet{wang2025dcsh} found that no single trace representation consistently outperforms others on generation-oriented tasks, concluding that the utility of execution traces is task- and format-dependent.
However, their study focused on code generation and repair---tasks that require the model to simulate or reconstruct execution semantics.
\emph{Verdict prediction}---classifying whether a test passes or fails---is a fundamentally different task type: it is a fault detection problem, not a generation problem.
Whether the same trace components matter for fault detection as for generation is unknown.

We present the first systematic study of what trace components drive verdict prediction performance.
Using 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} and MBPP-sanitized \citep{austin2021program} with model-generated solutions and execution traces, we decompose a multi-component trace representation (VOTA: exception events + assertion-point comparisons + loop compression) into individual components and evaluate each in isolation across two models: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct.

Our results reveal a striking finding: \textbf{exception events alone are sufficient for near-perfect verdict prediction, and this signal transfers across model families.}
With only exception events as trace input, both models achieve ${\geq}$99.3\% accuracy (cross-model gap = 0.50 percentage points).
In contrast, the full VOTA representation---which combines exception events with assertion-point and loop information---degrades by 14.96pp on the weaker model, indicating that processing mixed trace components demands model capability that exception-only prediction does not.

These results reframe verdict prediction as fault detection: the minimal sufficient signal is the exception event, a compact structured diagnostic moment that both models can interpret without deep trace reasoning.
We further decompose the gap between full trace and VOTA into two mechanisms---\emph{gradient dilution} (26\% of the gap) and \emph{information overload} (74\%)---showing that the primary bottleneck is not training signal quality but the presence of irrelevant trace content.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Exception signal universality}: We show that exception events alone achieve 99.83\%/99.33\% accuracy across two models (gap = 0.50pp), while VOTA degrades 14.96pp on the weaker model (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
\item \textbf{Information density decomposition}: We decompose the full-trace-to-VOTA gap into gradient dilution (26\%) and information overload (74\%), identifying the primary bottleneck for trace-based prediction (\S\ref{sec:density}).
\item \textbf{Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy}: Component ablation reveals that Tier~1 signals (exception events, assertion points) individually achieve ${\geq}$99.8\% accuracy while Tier~2 signals (loop compression) reach only 85.6\% (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Method}
2	
3	\subsection{Task Definition}
4	
5	We study \emph{verdict prediction}: given a Python function, a test input, and an optional execution trace, predict whether the test passes or fails.
6	The model produces a single token---\texttt{pass} or \texttt{fail}---making this a binary classification task.
7	Unlike code generation \citep{chen2025tracepile} or output prediction \citep{gu2024cruxeval}, verdict prediction isolates the model's ability to detect faults from its ability to simulate execution, providing a cleaner lens on what trace information actually contributes.
8	
9	\subsection{Dataset}
10	\label{sec:dataset}
11	
12	We sampled 10 candidate solutions per problem from Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (temperature 0.8, top\_p 0.95) for 591 problems from HumanEval \citep{chen2021evaluating} (164 problems) and MBPP-sanitized \citep{austin2021program} (427 problems), executed each solution against canonical test cases with \texttt{sys.settrace} to obtain line-level execution traces and pass/fail verdicts, yielding 5,910 trace--verdict pairs (67\% pass, 33\% fail).
13	The dataset is split 80/20 by problem ID into 4,720 training and 1,190 test samples; the test set majority-class baseline is 71.51\%.
14	
15	\subsection{Trace Representations}
16	
17	We define seven input conditions that systematically vary the trace information available to the model (Figure~\ref{fig:trace_overview}):
18	
19	\begin{itemize}
20	\item \texttt{no\_trace}: Source code and test input only; no execution information.
21	\item \texttt{full\_trace}: Complete line-by-line execution trace recording variable states at each step.
22	\item \texttt{VOTA} (Verdict-Oriented Trace Abstraction): Three compressed components---exception events, assertion-point comparisons, and loop compression summaries.
23	\item \texttt{exception\_only}: Only exception and error events extracted from the trace (e.g., \texttt{[ERROR] TypeError: ...}).
24	\item \texttt{ae\_only}: Only assertion-point actual/expected value pairs from the final comparison.
25	\item \texttt{loop\_only}: Only loop compression summaries (iteration counts and final variable states).
26	\item \texttt{VOTA\_no\_ae}: VOTA without assertion-point information (exception events + loop compression).
27	\end{itemize}
28	
29	These conditions span a spectrum from no trace information (\texttt{no\_trace}) through maximally compressed signals (\texttt{exception\_only}) to the complete unfiltered trace (\texttt{full\_trace}).
30	
31	\begin{figure*}[t]
32	\centering
33	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig1_trace_overview}
34	\caption{Overview of the verdict prediction pipeline. Source code and a test input are executed to produce a full raw trace. Four experimental conditions vary the trace information provided to the model: \texttt{no\_trace} (code only, 75.13\%), \texttt{full\_trace} (complete trace, 81.76\%), VOTA (compressed components, 99.41\%), and \texttt{exception\_only} (exception events only, 99.83\%). Each condition is paired with the same model to predict a pass/fail verdict. Accuracies shown are for Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B (seed=42, $N{=}1{,}190$).}
35	\label{fig:trace_overview}
36	\end{figure*}
37	
38	\subsection{Models}
39	
40	We evaluate two instruction-tuned code LLMs at the 7B parameter scale:
41	
42	\begin{itemize}
43	\item \textbf{Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct} \citep{qwen2025coder}: Pretrained on 5.5T tokens. Serves as the primary model for all ablation experiments.
44	\item \textbf{DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct} \citep{deepseek2024coder}: Pretrained on 2T tokens. Used for cross-model validation to test whether findings generalize beyond a single model family.
45	\end{itemize}
46	
47	The two models differ primarily in pretraining data volume (5.5T vs.\ 2T tokens), providing a natural axis for evaluating whether trace signal utility is model-dependent \citep{dong2024composition}.
48	
49	\subsection{Training Setup}
50	
51	All conditions use identical training configurations to ensure fair comparison.
52	We apply LoRA \citep{hu2022lora} (rank=16, $\alpha$=32, dropout=0.05) to all linear layers and train for 3 epochs with batch size 4, gradient accumulation 8 (effective batch size 32), learning rate $2 \times 10^{-4}$ with linear warmup and linear decay, warmup ratio 0.1, and weight decay 0.01.
53	The maximum sequence length is 2,048 tokens; input sequences exceeding this limit are truncated from the input content while preserving the complete verdict label.
54	Training wall-clock time ranges from 0.5 to 2.5 hours per condition on a single GPU, depending on trace format verbosity.
55	The primary seed is 42; seed robustness is evaluated with seeds 123 and 456 for the \texttt{exception\_only} condition.
56	
57	\subsection{Loss Ablation}
58	
59	To disentangle training signal quality from input signal quality, we introduce a \texttt{full\_trace\_label\_only} variant.
60	This condition uses the same full trace as input but computes loss only on the verdict token, masking all trace tokens during training (loss weight = 0 on trace positions).
61	If this variant improves over standard \texttt{full\_trace}, the improvement is attributable to \emph{gradient dilution}---trace tokens diluting the training signal without contributing to verdict prediction.
62	The remaining gap to VOTA is then attributable to \emph{information overload}---irrelevant trace content that the model must process at inference time.

11	The Tier~1 accuracy of ${\geq}$99.8\% is therefore unsurprising in isolation.

13

15	
16	The cross-model gap pattern (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a design principle: \emph{trace representations should match the model capability floor, not the ceiling.}
17	Exception events transfer across models precisely because they are structurally simple---a fixed-format error message that any instruction-tuned model can pattern-match.
18	VOTA's richer representation (loop summaries, assertion comparisons) requires compositional reasoning over heterogeneous formats, which the smaller DeepSeek model (2T pretrain tokens) cannot reliably perform---consistent with findings that SFT generalization depends heavily on base model capability \citep{yang2024generalization}.
19	The practical implication is that trace-based systems should default to the simplest sufficient signal, reserving richer representations for tasks that demonstrably require them.

22

24	This 0.50pp drop means that the cross-model gap under \texttt{exception\_only} is 0pp at best checkpoint and 0.50pp at final checkpoint.
25	Both values are negligible, but the pattern has practical implications: continued training on a near-solved task can introduce overfitting to spurious correlations in the training set, degrading performance on the small number of ambiguous samples.
26	This is consistent with the observation that exception events provide such a strong signal that the model ``solves'' the task early; subsequent epochs optimize for marginal training loss reduction at the expense of generalization.
27	The contrast with VOTA is stark---DeepSeek VOTA accuracy does not exhibit this non-monotonic pattern, suggesting that the weaker model never fully learns the VOTA signal and thus does not overfit to it.

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{Why Exception Events Dominate}

Verdict prediction is fundamentally a fault detection task: the model must determine whether execution deviated from expected behavior.
Exception events are the most explicit signal of such deviation---structured diagnostic moments that encode the nature and location of a fault.
Unlike loop compressions or assertion-point values, which require the model to integrate information across multiple trace elements, exception events provide a self-contained verdict cue.
This explains why \texttt{exception\_only} matches or exceeds VOTA: adding non-exception trace components dilutes the model's attention on the diagnostic signal rather than providing complementary information.

We acknowledge that exception-based verdict prediction is, at its core, fault indicator presence detection: the model learns to map the presence or absence of a structured error message to a binary label, which is close to trivially solvable for any instruction-tuned LLM.
The Tier~1 accuracy of ${\geq}$99.8\% is therefore unsurprising in isolation.
The contribution of this finding lies not in demonstrating that a strong signal yields high accuracy, but in two less obvious results: (a)~adding more trace information---loop compressions, assertion-point values---actively \emph{hurts} performance (VOTA $<$ \texttt{exception\_only}, Table~\ref{tab:ablation}), quantifying an information density dilution effect that has not been previously measured; and (b)~this dilution is model-dependent, with DeepSeek VOTA fail recall collapsing to 45.43\% (Table~\ref{tab:per_class}) while Qwen maintains 100\%, revealing that mixed-signal trace processing amplifies capability gaps between models.

\subsection{Simplicity as Robustness}

The cross-model gap pattern (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a design principle: \emph{trace representations should match the model capability floor, not the ceiling.}
Exception events transfer across models precisely because they are structurally simple---a fixed-format error message that any instruction-tuned model can pattern-match.
VOTA's richer representation (loop summaries, assertion comparisons) requires compositional reasoning over heterogeneous formats, which the smaller DeepSeek model (2T pretrain tokens) cannot reliably perform---consistent with findings that SFT generalization depends heavily on base model capability \citep{yang2024generalization}.
The practical implication is that trace-based systems should default to the simplest sufficient signal, reserving richer representations for tasks that demonstrably require them.

\subsection{Checkpoint Selection and Signal Stability}

The DeepSeek \texttt{exception\_only} result reveals an instructive training dynamic: accuracy peaked at 99.83\% after epoch~1 but degraded to 99.33\% at convergence (epoch~3).
This 0.50pp drop means that the cross-model gap under \texttt{exception\_only} is 0pp at best checkpoint and 0.50pp at final checkpoint.
Both values are negligible, but the pattern has practical implications: continued training on a near-solved task can introduce overfitting to spurious correlations in the training set, degrading performance on the small number of ambiguous samples.
This is consistent with the observation that exception events provide such a strong signal that the model ``solves'' the task early; subsequent epochs optimize for marginal training loss reduction at the expense of generalization.
The contrast with VOTA is stark---DeepSeek VOTA accuracy does not exhibit this non-monotonic pattern, suggesting that the weaker model never fully learns the VOTA signal and thus does not overfit to it.
For deployment, this finding recommends early stopping or best-checkpoint selection when fine-tuning on high-signal trace conditions, rather than training to convergence.

\subsection{Error Analysis}
\label{sec:error_analysis}

Seed robustness testing revealed that the two errors made by \texttt{exception\_only} (accuracy = 99.83\%, 2/1190 incorrect) are \emph{identical across all three seeds} (42, 123, 456).
Both errors are false negatives on samples involving the \texttt{check\_dict\_case} function (sample IDs 901 and 905): the ground truth is \texttt{pass}, but the model predicts \texttt{fail}.
This 100\% error overlap ($\sigma{=}0$) across seeds demonstrates that these are not stochastic training artifacts but \emph{irreducible samples} at the boundary of what exception-based trace signals can resolve.

We hypothesize that \texttt{check\_dict\_case} generates no exception events on passing inputs (correct behavior produces no errors), leaving the model without a distinguishing trace signal.
The model defaults to predicting \texttt{fail}---a reasonable heuristic when exception-based evidence is absent, since most trace-bearing inputs contain exception events precisely because they fail.
This systematic error pattern confirms that the two misclassifications represent a capability boundary of the exception-only format rather than a training instability, and that the 99.83\% accuracy is a deterministic ceiling for this trace representation on this dataset.

\subsection{Limitations}

Our study has several limitations.
First, all experiments use a single dataset (591 problems from HumanEval and MBPP-sanitized); generalization to other languages, larger codebases, or different fault types remains untested.
Second, we evaluate only two models at the 7B parameter scale; the relationship between model size and trace signal utility is unexplored.
Third, the \texttt{exception\_only} seed robustness is confirmed (3 seeds, $\sigma{=}0$), but other conditions use a single seed.
Fourth, the DeepSeek \texttt{full\_trace} condition was invalidated because the DeepSeek tokenizer produced sequences exceeding 2,048 tokens, causing the verdict label to be truncated during training; the model consequently failed to learn the classification task, and we report it as N/A rather than presenting potentially misleading results.
Finally, our analysis is limited to verdict prediction; whether exception dominance extends to other classification tasks (vulnerability detection, clone detection) or to generation tasks (program repair) is an open question.
